title: Pistachio and rose layer cake
subtitle: pistachio sponge with rose-scented buttercream
excerpt: A pistachio and rose layer cake combines a pale green ground-pistachio sponge with a delicate rose buttercream and a finish of whole pistachio pieces and dried rose petals. The sponge is moist and nutty; the frosting is subtly floral without tasting perfumed. The pairing of pistachios and rose water is a classic Persian and Middle Eastern combination that translates well into a Western celebration cake format.
sourceNotes: Pistachio and rose water appear together in Persian, Turkish, and Middle Eastern confectionery from at least the medieval period, where the combination is found in baklava, Turkish delight, and the cardamom-scented sweets of the Mughal court. The pairing entered mainstream British and American baking via the Persian-influenced recipes of Claudia Roden, Yotam Ottolenghi, and their successors. The layer cake format here is entirely Western; the flavour profile is Middle Eastern.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze unfrosted layers well wrapped for up to 2 months.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake the sponge layers a day ahead; frost on the day.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional 170°C or fan 150°C; the pistachio sponge bakes slower than a flour sponge; test with a skewer

content.text: Pistachio and rose layer cake has a naturally pale green sponge made from blitzed pistachios and a lightly floral rose buttercream. The rose water in the frosting should be subtle, start with a small amount and taste before adding more; some brands are stronger than others. The dried rose petals scattered on top make the flavour obvious on first look.

items.prepNote: start with 1 tbsp; add more to taste

content.text: Preheat the oven to 170°C conventional (150°C fan). Grease and line three 18 cm round tins. Blitz the pistachios and 50 g of the caster sugar in a food processor to a fine meal. Beat the butter and remaining 200 g caster sugar until pale and fluffy. Add the eggs one at a time. Fold in the pistachio meal and baking powder until combined. Divide evenly among the three tins and bake for 25 to 30 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool on a wire rack.

Beat the butter until pale. Add the sifted icing sugar in two additions with the milk, beating well after each. Add 1 tablespoon of rose water, beat to combine, then taste. Add more rose water gradually, the level you want is present but not overpowering. Assemble the three layers with buttercream between each, then cover the outside with a smooth final coat. Decorate the top with chopped pistachios and dried rose petals.
